newsitem.title: UK: London precious metal come off lows in afternoon.
newsitem.headline: London precious metal come off lows in afternoon.

text.p: A fresh bout of speculative buying lifted precious metals prices on Friday afternoon, although volumes were light, dealers said.
Gold was fixed at $352.80 an ounce on Friday afternoon, compared to $351.70 in the morning and Thursday's London close of $351.40/$351.90.
Meanwhile palladium prices shot up to a high of $154.50/$155.50, some $6 up from the day's low.
"The funds out of New York are back again into palladium, whipping it around. That's helping gold along with a weaker dollar," a dealer said.
Platinum was also off the days lows, while silver was back on par with Thursday's London close after shrugging off a downside probe earlier in the day.
Volumes were light in all the precious metals which was helping exaggerate price movements.
"If it wasn't so quiet it would be quite an interesting time with all these factors coming next week," one dealer said.
What might have resulted in a Comex-led rally on Thursday was truncated by U.S. Reserve Board chairman Alan Greenspan strongly hinting at upcoming rises in U.S. interest rates.
The monetary policy advising Federal Open market Committee (FOMC) meets next week and a 25 basis point rise has been forecast.
"Unless there is much bigger rate rise than that, gold should be unaffected," one dealer said.
Gold was forecast to remain fairly whippy but confined to a tight range bounded by $350.00-$355.00 at the outside.
The expiry of over-the-counter options next Tuesday may help give the market direction next week, dealers said.
"The feeling is that after the options expire, the price will move lower, but there is no keen view," a dealer said.
Palladium started the day weaker after being hit by currency-related selling by Japanese speculators during Asian trading hours, dealers said.
But the market is still jittery and easily buffeted by speculators, due to delayed supply contract talks between producer Russia and key importer Japan.
A Russian precious metals official said on Friday that it was unclear when talks on Russian supply contract talks with Japan would begin or when deliveries would start.
Platinum, at $378.00/$379.00, was down $1.95, while silver was up one cent from Thursday's finish at $5.18/$5.20.
